    Hi, I’m Jake Sansom

    Welcome to my homepage! I am a Ph.D. student studying both computer and cognitive science at the University of Michigan. I am co-advised by Professors Joyce Chai and Honglak Lee. I aim to computationally model the reasoning processes and memory systems that enable humans to learn from direct instruction and small amounts of experience.

    Curriculum Vitae

    Here is a link to my curriculum vitae. (Last updated November 2025)

    Highlights

    • [Paper Link] My current project, focused on evaluating LLMs’ ability to learn via naturalistic interactions with human users, was recently accepted into the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Multi-Turn Interactions in LLMs.
    • [Paper Link] I helped publish a paper in ACL 2025 that utilizes Read-Eval-Print Loops (REPLs) to structure LLM planning on a variety of domains.
    • [Paper Link] I helped publish a paper at EMNLP 2023 on LLMs’ capacity for Theory of Mind (reasoning about the mental states of others).

    Brief Biography

    I was born in Austin, TX, raised in Birmingham, AL, and subsequently returned to Texas to attend the University of Texas at Austin (Hook’em Horns!). While there, I studied computational engineering, a degree program focused on numerical methods for the simulation of physical phenomena. Under the tutelage of Dr. Michael Sacks at the Willerson Center for Cardiovascular Modeling and Simulation, I spent two years developing computational models of heart tissue. Meanwhile, I began to cultivate a deep interest in cognitive science. I participated in the Polymathic Scholars Honors Program, which enabled me to hand-design a field of study which I called “Architecture of the Mind.” This work culminated in my senior thesis, which I wrote under the advice of Dr. Michael Mauk. After college I spent two years in San Diego, CA working for Northrop Grumman. While there, I had the opportunity to work on a variety of products, most of which leveraged my knowledge of digital signal processing. In September of 2022, I decided to return both to school and to my love of cognitive science to obtain my master’s degree in computer science from the University of Michigan. I am now pursuing both a Ph.D. in computer science and a certificate in cognitive science.

    When not working, I enjoy staying active by running and cycling.
